title: Time and Physical Geometry
version: The Journal of Philosophy 64(8) (1967), pp. 240-247. Text retrieved this run from a publicly posted JSTOR scan (weebly-hosted PDF, OCR spacing normalized); official PDCnet/JSTOR records confirm metadata. Consistent with knowledge/foundations full-text audit record found-putnam.
relevance: Primary anchor for Contract E (whole-history eternalism): thesis (1) foil, assumptions i-ii, Principle III, reality transfer, tenseless-existence conclusion, anti-absolute-simultaneity clause.
limits: Quotes are short excerpts (research quotation); OCR spacing artifacts normalized without changing wording. Putnam's future-contingent truth-value step (pp. 243-246) is recorded as his stronger separate argument, not as part of the existence route.
locator: thesis (1) p. 240; assumptions i-ii p. 240; Principle III p. 241; transfer application pp. 241-243; transitive closure and 'enough observers' p. 246; tenseless-existence coextension pp. 246-247; 'four-dimensional and not a three-dimensional world' p. 246; 'no longer any philosophical problems about Time' p. 247
assumptions: Man-on-street thesis (1) as foil; I-now real; another moving observer real; Principle III (no privileged observers) restricted to tenseless, coordinate-independent physical R
conclusion: On natural choices of R in SR, future (and past) things are real though they do not exist now; 'real' is coextensive with tenseless existence; a privileged-frame reading would define an absolute simultaneity and is rejected
proof_status: Argumentative essay; the foundations lane audited it at full-text depth and marked the conclusion as not entailed by Lorentz kinematics alone (bridge premise)
open_questions: Whether Principle III survives as a defensible bridge premise (routed to bridge-premises lane)
Whether Stein 1991's automorphism-invariance condition is the same neutrality constraint

title: Scientific Thought
version: London: Kegan Paul, Trench, Trubner / New York: Harcourt, Brace, 1923. Internet Archive item scientificthough00broauoft (University of Toronto scan); djvu.txt OCR downloaded and searched this run. Key passage verified verbatim (OCR double-spacing and end-of-line hyphenation normalized).
relevance: Primary anchor for Contract G (growing block): reality of present+past, future 'simply nothing at all', sum total of existence increasing, Becoming as the third kind of change; also the classical growing life-history picture of persistence.
limits: Only the Ch. 2 time-and-change passages (printed pp. 43-68 region; exact passage pp. 66-68) were inspected this run; the rest of the book is unread. OCR errors possible in surrounding text; the quoted clause was checked word-by-word against the SEP quotation (independent transcription).
locator: printed pp. 66-68: 'accepts the reality of the present and the past, but holds that the future is simply nothing at all'; 'Nothing has happened to the present by becoming past except that fresh slices of existence have been added'; 'The sum total of existence is always increasing'; 'A moment t is later than a moment t' if the sum total of existence at t includes ... something more'; 'a complete analysis ... involve[s] the coming into existence of events. Let us call the third kind of change Becoming'; 'A Specious Present of mine is just the last thin slice that has joined up to my life-history'
assumptions: Absolute (Newtonian) time order; events as particulars that come into existence
conclusion: Growth of the sum total of existence grounds temporal direction (sense as well as order) and underlies attribute-change and pastward change
proof_status: Philosophical argument; no formalism in the quoted passage
open_questions: Broad's later refinements (1938 Examination of McTaggart vol. II, 'The Accidental Future') unread
Whether Broad's own framework supports the preferred-slicing relativistic variant or only the classical one (we claim the latter, with the slicing supplied by Bell-type or cosmic-time premises)

title: How to teach special relativity
version: Reprint in 'Speakable and Unspeakable in Quantum Mechanics' (CUP 1987), pp. 67-80 (first published 1976, Internationales Einstein-Symposium, Bern); publicly hosted PDF read via text extraction this run; printed page header 77 confirmed for the quoted passage.
relevance: Primary anchor for Contract G's Lorentzian preferred-frame premise: a real rest state defined by the aether that the laws conspire to hide; explicitly offered as pedagogy separable from Lorentz's philosophy.
limits: Only the opening and closing sections inspected this run; the full essay's dynamical details not re-read. Hosted PDF is a scan; wording checked against two extraction passes.
locator: printed p. 77: 'Lorentz ... preferred the view that there is indeed a state of real rest, defined by the aether, even though the laws of physics conspire to prevent us identifying it experimentally. The facts of physics do not oblige us to accept one philosophy rather than the other. And we need not accept Lorentz's philosophy to accept a Lorentzian pedagogy.'
assumptions: Lorentz-invariant laws expressed in one frame; moving observers and their instruments derived from those laws
conclusion: Single-frame formulation accounts for all appearances; preference for a real rest frame is philosophical, not experimentally forced
open_questions: Whether a Bell-style real rest frame plus Broad growth yields a coherent relativistic GBT (our Contract G), and what Earman 2008's non-cheating objection does to it

relevance: Nearest physics-motivated growth view (evolving block universe); recorded to keep Contract G honest: Ellis explicitly locates growth in proper time along worldline families, NOT preferred surfaces.
limits: Paper body not extracted this run (two fetch attempts returned abstract/references only). No body-text clause is quoted; the abstract clause is exact.
locator: abstract (v5): 'the unchanging block universe view of spacetime is best replaced by an evolving block universe ... However this time evolution is not related to any preferred surfaces in spacetime; rather it is associated with the evolution of proper time along families of world lines'
assumptions: Macro-emergent complexity taken as real; micro time-reversibility not decisive for ontology
conclusion: Evolving block universe with worldline-based (not surface-based) present; potential becomes certainty of the past
proof_status: Physico-philosophical proposal; no theorem claimed in the abstract
open_questions: Body-text clauses on the crystallizing boundary (gate)
Whether Ellis 2012 'meshing together of times' changes the worldline/surface balance
